draft.title: Homeostasis and negative feedback
card: Homeostasis keeps conditions inside the body steady. Negative feedback is how it does so: a change triggers a response that reverses it.
Each condition has a set point, its normal level. If the body gets too hot, sweating cools it down. Once the temperature returns to the set point, the response eases off.
If the body gets too cold, shivering makes muscles release heat and warms it up.
The word negative does not mean bad. It means the response works against the change, so conditions move back towards the set point.
draft.remember: Homeostasis uses negative feedback to return a condition to its set point.

a.q: A condition in the body rises above its set point. What does negative feedback do?
opts: Causes a response that brings it back down
Causes a response that pushes it up further
Stops the body from detecting the change
Leaves it high until the stimulus ends
a.why: Negative feedback reverses the change, so a rise leads to a response that lowers the condition. Pushing it up further would make the change bigger, which is not what negative feedback does.
a.clue: Negative means working against the change.

b.q: Priya has been standing in a cold pool in Victoria and begins to shiver. How does shivering show negative feedback?
opts: It warms her body, reversing the fall in temperature
It cools her body, reversing the fall in temperature
It warms her body, making the cold change bigger
It shows her body has stopped detecting the cold
b.why: Shivering makes muscles release heat, which reverses the drop in body temperature. It is not a bad response just because she feels uncomfortable: it works against the change.
b.clue: Which response works against the cold?

a.best: Causes a response that brings it back down

b.best: It warms her body, reversing the fall in temperature
